subject: MAP kickoff + hosting evaluation: PulseCare deployment options (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@pulsecare.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.shah@pulsecare.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 16:12:00 -0500
Subject: Kickoff: MAP & hosting evaluation for PulseCare

Hi Sofia / Michael,

Thanks for the intro call earlier — attaching our initial MAP (PulseCare_MAP_v0.9.xlsx) with dates and internal milestones. High-level asks from our side:
- We need to finalize hosting mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) by mid-December so engineering can lock network requirements.
- Compliance: HIPAA + SOC2 evidence required before pilot.
- Region: US-only for PHI (preference: us-east for latency into our east-coast customers).

Key milestone we’re targeting: pilot (limited patient data) week of Jan 15 2027, GA March 1. Can Redwood support a dedicated-capacity pilot or would Private (VPC/air-gapped) be necessary for the pilot?

I’ve CC’d Priya (security lead) and Karthik from your SE team per the call notes.

Attachments: PulseCare_MAP_v0.9.xlsx (MAP draft)

Thanks,
Alex Moreno
Head of Product, PulseCare Systems
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@pulsecare.com>
Cc: michael_grant@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Kickoff: MAP & hosting evaluation for PulseCare

Alex — thanks for the MAP and the clear milestones. I uploaded a Redwood MAP template and populated an initial proposed timeline and ownership columns (attached: Redwood_MAP_template.xlsx).

Quick answers up front:
- Hosted (shared) is fastest to get started but likely not acceptable for PHI at scale.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pool + customer VPC peering) is a common middle ground — we can offer a dedicated pilot with data isolation and an SLA.
- Private (customer-managed private deployment / on-prem) is available for customers with strict control requirements but adds ~6–8 weeks for provisioning and hardening.

Proposed next steps:
1) Security Q&A: Priya, can you share your SOC2 checklist and any minimum requirements?
2) Technical spike: Karthik — can your team outline a short perf plan (latency, throughput, KV-cache expectations) for the pilot dataset?
3) Decision checkpoint: target 2026-12-15 for final hosting selection so procurement can start the SOW.

I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up Thursday to walk the MAP and proposed evaluation tests.

— Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@pulsecare.com>
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
Cc: priya.shah@pulsecare.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:21:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Kickoff: MAP & hosting evaluation for PulseCare

Thanks Sofia — that matches our expectation. A couple of technical/security clarifications before Thursday:
- SOC2: we will need evidence around log retention and access controls. Priya, can you start a list of docs you need?
- Encryption: At-rest + in-transit required; do you support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for Dedicated?
- Private option: would on-prem require code changes or is it a packaging + networking exercise? Roughly how long to spin up?

Also attaching a schema extract (PulseCare_test_schema.csv) with a few sample (anonymized) rows — we can make a sanitized test set available for the pilot if Redwood signs a data processing addendum.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alex
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, michael_grant@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0500
Subject: Internal: PulseCare hosting decision — evaluation checklist and responsibilities

Team — summary and proposed evaluation plan (internal draft):

Objective: validate whether Dedicated (with VPC peering + customer KMS) meets PulseCare’s PHI and SLA requirements, or whether Private deployment is required.

Evaluation checkpoints (to complete by 2026-12-13):
- Security: SOC2 artifacts, key management (KMS), network isolation verification — owner: Michael
- Performance: 95th pct latency with 2k concurrent small requests, throughput baseline, KV cache hit-rate — owner: Karthik
- Operational: SLOs for failover, autoscaling test plan, monitoring/trace integration — owner: Sofia
- Procurement: SOW stub and pricing for dedicated monthly commit vs private deployment fix-cost — owner: Sofia (coordinate with finance)

Suggested acceptance criteria for Dedicated pilot:
- Data-in-transit & at-rest encryption with customer KMS
- Audit logs accessible for 90 days (can extend)
- Baseline 95th pct latency < 180ms for test workload in us-east

Rough cost bands (for decision conversation):
- Hosted: lowest up-front, not recommended for PHI at production volumes
- Dedicated pilot: ~$45–70k/month (pilot rate, depends on commit)
- Private/on-prem: ~$180k one-time provisioning + ops premium

I’ll turn this into a populated MAP tab and send to Alex with the ask list and a suggested SOW stub.

— Sofia
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@pulsecare.com>, sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0500
Subject: MAP v1 + Dec PoC week proposal (PulseCare)

Alex / Priya — attaching an updated MAP (PulseCare_MAP_v1.xlsx) that includes the evaluation checkpoints and a security evidence request (SOC2_evidence_request.pdf).

Immediate asks from PulseCare to unblock the PoC:
- Please sign the DPA and the PoC SOW stub (DocuSign link below) — this will allow us to ingest the anonymized test set.
- Provide access to the anonymized test set (PulseCare_test_schema.csv) via secure SFTP or a shared bucket with limited TTL.

Proposed PoC week: Dec 13–17 (we’ll reserve a dedicated GPU pool and run the performance scripts). KPIs we’ll measure during the week: cold-start p95, steady-state throughput, and prefix-cache hit rate.
